subject: Computer Networking
title: Slack's Boot Loop (2021)
description: A micro-lesson that makes Slack's Boot Loop (2021) usable.

hook.text: On January 4, 2021 — the first workday of the year — Slack crashed as everyone logged back in.

buildup.text: Millions of remote workers returned from holiday break and opened Slack at once. The traffic spike was massive.

discovery.text: Slack's infrastructure couldn't handle the surge. Auto-scaling tried to help but hit internal limits.

twist.text: The outage lasted hours. For fully remote companies, losing Slack meant losing all internal communication.

climax.text: The incident exposed a single point of failure in remote work: the one chat tool everyone depends on.

punchline.text: Everyone came back to work at once. Slack wasn't ready.

quiz.question: What caused Slack's January 2021 outage?
options: A massive traffic spike when millions returned from holiday
A ransomware attack on Slack's servers

details.summary: In January 2021, Slack experienced a major outage when millions of users returned to work after the holidays simultaneously. The surge in connections overwhelmed Slack's infrastructure, creating a boot loop where servers crashed, restarted, and crashed again under the reconnection flood.
details.whyItMatters: Slack's outage demonstrated the thundering herd problem: when millions of clients reconnect simultaneously, the recovery traffic can be worse than the original failure.
takeaways: Millions of simultaneous reconnections overwhelmed Slack
The thundering herd problem amplified the initial failure
Slack added exponential backoff and progressive reconnection

faq.question: What is the thundering herd problem?
faq.answer: When a service recovers from a failure, all disconnected clients try to reconnect simultaneously. This reconnection flood can exceed the original traffic that caused the failure, crashing the service again. The cycle repeats until the herd is managed with staggered reconnection.

faq.question: How did Slack prevent this from happening again?
faq.answer: They implemented progressive reconnection with randomized delays so clients do not all reconnect at once. They added capacity headroom for peak reconnection scenarios and improved their load shedding to gracefully reject excess connections during recovery.
